content.thinking:
I'll write the whole file carefully in one pass, keeping things robust with plain geometric primitives like boxes, cones, lathes, and sweeps since it's a diorama with no moving parts needing a skeleton. I still need at least one root joint, so I'll add a base joint at the origin and attach unparented parts to the nearest one.

For the design, I'm planning an oasis scene roughly 2.6m across: a blob-shaped sand base, a turquoise pool with rim stones, waterfall rocks, three palms, two tents, two camels, a campfire, crates, jars, rugs, and plants, all built using helper functions for boxes with flat shading for a faceted low-poly look. I'm working out the extrusion math for the sand base outline in the XZ plane and layering the pool surface just above it with its own thin extrusion and stone border.

I need the base outline to avoid self-intersection, so I'm generating it as a smooth polar function with 28 points. For the palms, I'm sweeping curved trunks with tapering radius and ring textures, then adding droopy fronds as leaf-shaped sweeps with elliptical cross-sections rotated around each trunk, plus orange sphere dates, and now I'm starting to figure out the tent structure with poles and a canopy in red and blue.

For the tent canopy, I'm designing it as an A-frame gable roof made from two angled thin box panels meeting at a ridge, computing the panel length and tilt angle from the width and height so each slopes correctly from the peak down to the sides, alongside a back wall and open curtained front.

I'll build a quaternion-based placement helper combining yaw with local rotation, then use it for painting stripe patterns on the roof and adding diamond-trim and rug textures via SVG planes positioned flat on the ground.

For camels, I'm planning simple capsule-and-sweep construction—horizontal body, S-curve neck, boxy head, four jointed legs—scaled down to roughly half a meter tall to match the miniature diorama proportions alongside the palms and tents.

Writing sweep geometry logic...

I'm baking a ground offset constant into the coordinate helper so everything sits properly on the sand, checking proportions against the palm scale. For the camel, I'm adding a blanket with striped texture, tassels, saddle bags, and reins, plus a lying variant with folded leg capsules and raised neck, and I'm starting the campfire with a stone ring and logs.

For props I'm sketching crates with wood-grain paint, lathe-banded jars, cheap spiky agave plants, and mottled rock shapes, plus a waterfall made from cliff rocks with a thin light-blue falling-water box and foam sphere. I need to keep the flat color palette modest, around 40 shared colors, since paints don't count against the 64-flat-color limit but random per-instance tints would blow past it.

Now I'm writing the actual code with strict typechecking in mind, watching for unused names.

Setting up builder helpers and local-frame transforms...

Adding more helper methods...

Now I'm sketching the overall layout coordinates: the pool at the center, waterfall cliff behind it, palms leaning outward behind the pool, and tents positioned on either side angled to face the center, with camels and a campfire placed toward the front.

Placing the campfire, stool, basket, and crates near the tents while checking they stay within the base radius. I'm defining the irregular base outline shape using a radius function with angular variation, then working out the extrusion mapping to convert the 2D outline into 3D world coordinates.

Writing paint functions for the sand base, using mottled coloring on top and layered strata stripes on the sides based on surface normal direction.

Then I'm adding a pool feature: an extruded ellipse outline filled with mottled teal-cyan water color, surrounded by a ring of gray-tan rim stones, plus a waterfall with cliff rock clusters and a falling water box behind it.

Now I'm building a palm tree generator: trunk curves from base to a leaning top using a catmull path with tapered radius and alternating bark-ring coloring, topped with a crown knob, date clusters, and ten fronds arcing outward at jittered angles via bezier curves.

I need to guard against negative values raised to fractional powers producing NaN, so I'll clamp with Math.max(0, ...). Now I'm designing the tent geometry function with width, depth, and ridge height parameters, building a hipped roof profile with vertical walls transitioning to sloped roof planes toward the ridge.

Computing the roof panel dimensions and rotation angles for each slope, then adding a stripe pattern texture to the roof surface for visual detail.

For the back wall, I'm planning a pentagon-shaped extruded outline to form the gable shape, computing the local direction vectors by applying the tent's rotation quaternion so the wall aligns properly with the overall orientation.

Now I'm adding side walls as simple boxes flanking the structure, plus interior details like a textured floor rug and front curtains rendered as thin sloped boxes along the gable edges in cream, topped with a decorative trim strip using a diamond-patterned plane positioned and rotated to sit flush along the front roof edge.

Next I'm adding corner poles, ridge poles with gold finial balls, guy rods running from the eaves to ground stakes, small tassel cones at the eaves, and interior elements like cushions and a crate sitting on the rug.

Now I'm defining a camel-building function with color constants for the body, dark accents, and cream highlights, then starting to sweep a curved path to shape the camel's body.

Still writing body geometry...

Still placing legs, tail, and blanket panels...

Still shaping the halter and head geometry... and now sketching a lying-down camel pose with folded leg capsules and a rising neck curve made of swept segments.

I'm making the head a shared helper function so both standing and lying poses can reuse it with different base neck points, plus adding a rolled bedroll on the hump and stones for a campfire.

Now I'm building the campfire scene: a stone ring, logs, glowing flame cones, a tripod holding a pot over the fire, and simple furniture pieces like a stool, a woven basket with painted stripes, and lathe-generated jars using outline profiles.

Refining the jar silhouette coordinates, then adding paint logic for terracotta color with lighter decorative bands around specific height ranges.

Now I'm designing crates with wood grain texturing, dark metal corner bands, and a stacking function, plus agave plants built from rings of leaning spikes and simple dry grass tufts made of thin yellow-green blades.

Rocks come from scaled, flattened icosahedrons with mottled coloring and randomized rotation, sunk slightly into the ground, with bigger versions placed behind the waterfall pool. For rugs, I'm generating an SVG texture with a red field, border, and diamond pattern, then mapping it onto a thin plane positioned just above the ground with the correct orientation.

To lay the plane flat facing up, I rotate it -90 degrees on x so its normal points up, then apply yaw separately on top of that. I'll also make a matching diamond-pattern trim texture, add a small glowing lantern near the blue tent, and keep the total part count manageable around 400.

For the sphere parts I want faceted shading, so I'll mark them flat while keeping planes as they are, and I need to double-check the Fill type is properly imported for color parameters. For the palm tree, the trunk sits rooted in the sand, with frond details above and a cluster of orange date balls near the crown just below the fronds.

Now I'm working out the trunk's curved sweep path using a few interpolated points rising from base to top, tapering the radius as it goes, with alternating ring colors based on height for a segmented bark look.

I'm defining the outline point type and a helper to build tuple coordinates, then setting up the base extrusion centered on the ground plane with the correct thickness and orientation for the top face.

Now I'm determining paint logic for the top face normal, striped side painting for strata, and placing stones around the pool rim before assembling everything and returning the model root, sorting out typing for the sweep options along the way.

I'm writing the tent-building function with its roof and rod details, plus the striped roof texture logic accounting for world-axis rotation.

For the roof panel, I'll let the box geometry's UV mapping handle the baked paint texture across the surface. For interior details, I'm sizing a rug plane to match a portrait-oriented texture viewBox and positioning small maroon cushion boxes on the floor with slight rotation for a casual look.

I'm picking a color palette — gold, dark wood, red, blue, cream, teal — and planning a simple lantern built from a glowing box, cone roof, and ring to place near the crate instead of hanging it. Now I'm starting to define a helper function for building a camel's head using capsules and spheres for the skull, muzzle, and other features.

Still writing camel head geometry...

Still adding blanket details...

I'm checking that the hump and blanket positions clear the floor for both lying and standing camel poses, then sketching the reins path from the halter down to a chest ring with a rod.

With the rig done, I'm moving to final scattering: placing random plants, rocks, and sand pebbles around the scene while excluding an elliptical pool zone so nothing overlaps the water. Now I'll write the complete file.
